title: What are your current workflows for asset generation ?
author: Lalilalilaliho
selftext: Which AI tools are actually holding up for 3D asset generation right now? Feel like most of what I've tested still needs way too much manual cleanup for topology, PBR textures, and rigging to be viable in-engine.

comments.author: PositiveScarcity8909
comments.body: Chat Gpt design - Tripo - Claude topology check - Mixamo rigging/animation - Claude animation polish

comments.author: MichaelEmouse
comments.body:
Gemini for generating lots of images for free. These can be fed into ChatGPT or you can go to ChatGPT directly which is generally better for image generation. 

I use interactive evolution to generate many mutations at first. 

These can be fed into Claude, Tripo or Meshy. Meshy seems better for simpler or static objects or objects with a complex surfaces like a furry dog. Claude seems better for objects which must retain distinct parts and have many precise parts. 

You can look on YouTube for people making comparisons.

comments.author: CmdrCallandra
comments.body:
Since asset generation is always the one thing delaying development for me, I created a fully local 2d/3d asset generation tool with end to end workflow, rigging, full animation editor, textures, material edits, mesh cleanups, 3d to 2d pixel art, all such things.
Feel free to check it out at
https://github.com/SifuInTheShell/Effigy

replies.author: CmdrCallandra
replies.body: The workflows of effigy work atomic, which means in almost any step you can bring in what you like to. For example in your case, you can bring in your own image, let effigy remove background and generate 3d model from it. On characters you can then move on into rigging and animating. And if needed you can always bring the generated model into blender, work on it, and have it handed back over to effigy again. You could also do simpler work like Ai up scaling if needed. Easiest is probably to link your Ai agent via mcp against effigy and ask your agent to do those steps in sequence 😁

comments.author: gallo2fire
comments.body: I've found it's extremely helpful to give ai reference images to work from, this is actually where I see ai collaborating with me on the art side of things because I can mock up ideas and pull in images or other community free models and it seems to give it a better starting direction of the type of detail and model quality I'm looking for. After that I usually have it do a couple iterations on the model some by other ai's reviewing it and some by me telling exactly what parts need to be changed and how to change them. It's definitely not one shot and go but I find it more fun this way because I really feel like I'm using a tool to make what's in my head come to life. I only do this though for the most important models, if there's other models in the world that are a lower priority I'll give specific verticies size and texture constraints which helps give all those lower priority models a more cohesive look.

comments.author: deepinthewoods
comments.body:
SkinTokens for automatic rigging. Claude agents for making animations, they have a bunch of custom instructions based on my feedback, and python scripts for analyzing the animations. It still doesn't work that well.  I told her to research online about how to make like wing animations, how to make weapon attack animations etc and that's improved it quite a lot. Burns quite a lot of tokens doing the animations as well.

For the actual 3D models, I have a particular low poly style which I have my own custom polygon reduction system for. It's can use any high poly mesh from like meshy, tripo, hyper3d, etc. Hyper3d is the best at making lowpoly meshes, but it's expensive and i have 11 races, each need a bunch of outfits/armor. I just recently realized that the Google Gemini AI accounts have a bunch of credits for using Colab instances So I'm just using those to run Pixal3D Multi-view image to 3D conversion in the cloud. The way I do the outfits is I have blender renders of my base models from four different angles. They have the head and one Foot and one leg colored differently. Then I do a bunch of concept art with codex, Telling it to add outfits to the front view of the human male base model image. Then I pick the concept art I like. Tell Codex to put that outfit on the other angles of the base model and on the other races base models for all angles. So then I end up with four angles of every race, and they're based on the blender renders, so they're fairly dimensionally accurate. But it's still not perfect. Then I do multi-view image 3D with Tripo or whatever. I'm using Pixal3D via Colab now, which can do probably a thousand conversions or more with my twenty dollar subscription. Then I have some more processing steps for polygon reduction and also alignment. It uses the colored head and hand and foot to align The outfit models with the base model, That way the armor pieces line up with the base model well. I also generate one image with the with like a glove and a boot on the right hand side. I use that for gloves and boots, but mirrored. The other side I'm using for alignment. And then I generate a separate image with the actual body armor. And I convert them separately.

I tried doing procedural generation with Blender, but it never worked that well. I burned probably a month of claude usage on the $100 tier, and it never ended up looking that good. I had to give it loads of manual feedback. It just doesn't have the character of ImageGen. I'll get Claude to generate random words and incorporate those into the image generation prompt for codex and it makes some pretty interesting/weird stuff. Then I just pick the ones I like and make the multi-views for all the races based on those. Codex can generate about 1500 images per day on the $100 tier.

Furniture and stuff, weapons, tools I use ImageGen to generate like a grid of different ones. You can get a 3x3 or 4x4 grid pretty easy. Then get it get codex to generate a different angle of the same grid. Then image to 3D that and then I've got a bunch of props/weapons.

Buildings. I have a whole building editor in Godo that I can drive via Claude agents. So I can say to it, make the give this a more pointy roof or make it bigger or anything like that. And claude is able to drive the editor in Godot. Also Claude can operate my map editor and my dungeon editor in Godot based on my instructions. It's based on [WorldClaw](https://github.com/Tencent-Hunyuan/Hunyuan3D-WorldClaw).
